Subject: Mutual action playbook: hosting & region decision (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Emma / Oliver —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a first-pass mutual action playbook (MAP) that captures the evaluation plan, decision checkpoints, and a proposed close timeline so we can align on the Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision and the regional constraints. High-level asks from our side:

- Please confirm any binding data residency or processing restrictions (EU-only, specific country, or hybrid).
- Flag required security controls (KMS/HSM, SOC evidence, logging/audit retention).
- Confirm the target business milestone date you want Redwood fully available in production (you mentioned early Sept on the call).

Proposed next steps in the MAP (high level):
1) Finalize hosting mode decision (choose one): Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved EU pool), Private (VPC/on-prem).
2) Security verification & contract addenda (KMS, DPA language, procurement invoice entity) — legal + security loop.
3) PoC / evaluation (4w for Dedicated, 8–10w for Private, see attached).
4) Production cutover & SLA onboarding.

Target: decision by EOD Aug 24 so we can hit a Sept 10 production milestone if we choose Dedicated. If Private is required, we should plan for a later cutover and confirm procurement timeline now.

I attached Novamed_MAP_v1.xlsx that turns the bullets above into a dated mutual action checklist. Please review and share a single threaded response with any must-haves.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min sync after you review.

—

Subject: Re: Mutual action playbook: hosting & region decision (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Soojin —

Thanks for the deck and the clear checklist. A couple of quick points from NovaMed's side:

- Data residency: All clinical data must remain within the EU and be processed by an EU legal entity. We cannot send PHI outside the EU.
- KMS: We require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key or HSM-backed KMS).
- Compliance evidence: SOC 2 and penetration test report will need to be shared before procurement sign-off.
- Procurement: Invoices must be billed to NovaMed EU S.à r.l. (we will provide exact legal entity details).

Given these constraints, our initial preference is either: (A) Dedicated EU pool (Redwood-managed) with KMS integration, or (B) Private VPC hosted in our EU region. Hosted (multi-tenant) is likely a non-starter for production clinical data.

Can you confirm: which of these two options lets us hit a Sept 10 production milestone (or a meaningful pilot) assuming procurement & legal run in parallel?

—Emma
Emma Clarke
Head of Platform Integrations | NovaMed
emma.clarke@novamed.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@novamed.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action playbook: hosting & region decision (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Emma —

Thanks for the clarity. Quick summary and proposal so we have a concrete decision path:

Option A — Dedicated (EU-only reserved pool)
- Pros: Fastest to stand up (approx. 3–4 week PoC), Redwood manages infra, easy autoscaling within reserved capacity.
- Security: We can support customer-managed KMS via integration with your KMS (bring-your-own-key) for token-level encryption.
- Compliance evidence: SOC 2 + pen-test report available; will share redacted artifacts under NDA.
- Procurement/ops: Standard DE/EU invoice process supported.
- Estimated uplift: +25% over Hosted list price (reserved capacity premium).

Option B — Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Pros: Maximum data isolation and control.
- Cons: Longer lead time (approx. 8–10 weeks: network, KMS onboarding, Acceptance tests).
- Pricing: Platform license + setup fee.

Recommendation: If the goal is a Sept 10 pilot/initial production, choose Option A (Dedicated EU pool) and run a parallel Private evaluation if needed.

Action for NovaMed: Please confirm by EOD Aug 24 whether you want us to proceed with Dedicated EU pool provisioning. If yes, we will: 1) prepare a Dedicated PO estimate, 2) issue SOC2 docs (NDA), 3) schedule a technical kickoff for Aug 26.

I've also attached the Novamed_MAP_v1.xlsx with dates filled in per the two options (see attachments).

- Karthik

Emma / team —

Adding the evaluation & acceptance criteria we typically run for a customer PoC so everyone has the same success definition:

PoC scope (Dedicated EU pool):
- Inference throughput: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for our gen model under test load.
- Feature parity: streaming + tool-calls must be validated.
- Security: KMS integration tested for key rotate and audit logs.
- Data retention: logs retained for 90 days (configurable).
- Acceptance tests: 10 scripted prompts + 3 regression prompt sets supplied by NovaMed.

Operational cadence: weekly progress sync (30m), daily Slack channel during week 1 of PoC.

If you confirm Dedicated by Aug 24, we will reserve capacity and send a draft SOW/estimate for procurement.

—Laura
